content.text:
All 9 tests pass (`node --test`, exit 0).

**What was wrong in `duration.js`:**
- `parseDuration` used a global `/(
  - no validation at all: it scanned with a `g` regex, so anything unrecognized (`''`, `'1hxx30m'`, `'30m1h'`, `'1h2h'`) was silently skipped and it returned a number instead of throwing.
- `formatDuration(0)` returned `''` because zero parts joined to an empty string.

**Fix** (`/root/verify/pr12688/realmodel/runs/head-1/ws/duration.js`):
- Replaced the scanning loop with one anchored pattern, `^(?=\d)(?:(\d+)d)?(?:(\d+)h)?(?:(\d+)m)?(?:(\d+)s)?$`. The anchors reject stray characters; the fixed sequence of four distinct optional groups rejects both repeated units and out-of-order units; the `(?=\d)` lookahead rejects `''` without weakening the "one or more groups" requirement. Non-string input is caught by the `typeof` guard before the regex runs.
- Any miss throws `RangeError` with the offending value in the message.
- `formatDuration` now falls back to `'0s'` when no unit part is emitted.

**Verification beyond the suite:** I checked spec edges the tests don't cover — `'1h30'`, `'h5m'`, `'5'`, `'1x'`, `'1H'`, `'-1h'`, `' 1h'`, `'1s1m'`, `'1d1d'`, `'ms'`, `'\n'`, Arabic-Indic digits, plus `null`/`undefined`/`3600`/`{}`/`['1h']` all throw `RangeError`; `'0d0h0m0s'` → `0`; and formatting `59999 → '59s'`, `60000 → '1m'`, `93724000 → '1d2h3m4s'`, `864000000 → '10d'` behave as the canonical form requires. One anomaly in that check was my own wrong expectation (`'1h2m3s'` is valid, 3,723,000 ms), not an implementation defect. `duration.test.js` was not modified.
